title: [B2 • Band 6.0] Bài 304: The Mechanical Muse: AI and Art
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 304 (LEVEL B2 • BAND 6.0)

The Mechanical Muse: Artificial Intelligence and Aesthetic Value

Paragraph 1. In May 2018, an unremarkable portrait of a man in historic French dress sold at Christie's auction house in New York for $432,500—over forty times its pre-sale estimate. What fascinated collectors was not technical brilliance, but the artist's signature: an algebraic formula. Titled Portrait of Edmond de Belamy, the work was produced entirely by a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) trained on fifteen thousand historical portraits spanning six centuries. For technology enthusiasts, the sale announced a cultural turning point: machines had finally mastered human creativity.

Paragraph 2. In The Algorithmic Canvas, philosopher Dr. Julian Barnes mounts a sharp critique of this hype. He clarifies that a GAN functions via two rival algorithms: a 'generator' synthesizes digital images from random noise, while a 'discriminator' tests each output against a library of real human paintings, rejecting anything unconvincing. Through millions of iterations, the generator achieves statistical mimicry so polished that the discriminator cannot tell machine images from human works. Yet Barnes insists that labelling this computational pattern-matching 'creative' confuses mathematical imitation with genuine artistic intent.

Paragraph 3. True art, Barnes argues, requires artistic agency—conscious communication rooted in lived physical experience. When Vincent van Gogh painted The Starry Night, his restless brushstrokes did not average nineteenth-century colour statistics; they translated emotional pain, awe, and spiritual longing onto canvas. An algorithm, conversely, feels nothing, wants nothing, and experiences no mortality. It rearranges pixels mathematically without grasping that a pixel can signify grief, warmth, or love.

Paragraph 4. Beyond philosophy, Barnes highlights disturbing economic and cultural threats. If media corporations can produce infinite musical scores, articles, and illustrations at virtually zero marginal cost, the economic system sustaining living human creators will collapse. Even more damaging, generative algorithms train strictly on existing cultural archives, locking society inside an endless loop of past nostalgia and blending diverse tastes into a safe, predictable average.

Paragraph 5. While machines can remix historical styles at breathtaking speed, genuinely groundbreaking art demands breaking established conventions—a deliberate act of human rebellion that pure mathematics can never originate. Protecting authentic artistic culture therefore requires valuing conscious human expression above statistical mimicry.

groups.title: Questions 1–4
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer? Write YES, NO, or NOT GIVEN.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct ending, A–F, below.
endings: A. human creative professionals may no longer earn a living.
B. museum visitors prefer mathematical signatures over human names.
C. cultural diversity shrinks into a repetitive blend of older tastes.
D. one software module produces images while another evaluates them.
E. nineteenth-century artists regularly relied on statistical formulas.
F. human painters express conscious emotions rooted in real life.

groups.title: Questions 9–12
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

q1.text: The buyer of Portrait of Edmond de Belamy was a university computer professor.

steps: Đoạn 1: Chỉ nói bức tranh được bán đấu giá $432,500 tại Christie's, không nêu danh tính người mua.
Kết luận: NOT GIVEN.

q2.text: After many training cycles, a GAN generator can fool its discriminator program.

steps: Đoạn 2: Sau hàng triệu vòng lặp, bộ phân biệt không thể phân biệt ảnh máy với tranh thật.
Kết luận: YES.

q3.text: Advanced computer algorithms are starting to develop basic awareness of human mortality.

steps: Đoạn 3: Thuật toán không cảm nhận, không mong muốn và không có trải nghiệm sinh tử (experiences no mortality).
Kết luận: NO.

q4.text: Mass-produced AI art will raise average salaries for commercial illustrators.

steps: Đoạn 4: Hệ sinh thái kinh tế nuôi sống người sáng tạo sẽ sụp đổ (will collapse).
Kết luận: NO.
Đoạn 2: Một thuật toán tạo ảnh từ nhiễu ngẫu nhiên, thuật toán kia kiểm định đối chiếu tranh thật.
Đáp án: D.
Đoạn 3: Họa sĩ con người truyền tải cảm xúc có ý thức từ trải nghiệm sống thật.
Đáp án: F.

q7.text: When companies generate endless free content,

steps: Đoạn 4: Hệ thống kinh tế nuôi sống nghệ sĩ con người sẽ sụp đổ.
Đáp án: A.

q8.text: Because AI systems learn strictly from past archives,

steps: Đoạn 4: Mắc kẹt trong hoài niệm cũ, trộn thị hiếu đa dạng thành trung bình lặp lại.
Đáp án: C.

q9.text: Why did the 2018 Christie's auction attract global media attention?
options: A. It set the highest price ever paid for an oil portrait.
B. The painting had been missing from Paris for six centuries.
C. An artwork created completely by an algorithm sold for a huge sum.
D. The auction house donated all earnings to artificial intelligence labs.

steps: Đoạn 1: Tranh do thuật toán GAN vẽ hoàn toàn và ký tên công thức toán lại bán giá $432,500.
Đáp án: C.

q10.text: What does Van Gogh's The Starry Night demonstrate in Paragraph 3?
options: A. Authentic art conveys subjective emotional reality.
B. Classic painters calculated colour frequencies mathematically.
C. Mental suffering is necessary before anyone can paint well.
D. Oil brushstrokes cannot be shown clearly on digital screens.

steps: Đoạn 3: Tranh thật truyền tải nỗi đau, sự kinh ngạc và trải nghiệm cảm xúc chủ quan.
Đáp án: A.

q11.text: What economic danger does Dr. Barnes warn about in Paragraph 4?
options: A. Auction houses will close because digital paintings are too cheap.
B. Electricity costs for training AI will bankrupt media companies.
C. Traditional paint supplies will disappear from art colleges.
D. Zero-cost synthetic art could destroy livelihoods for human creators.

steps: Đoạn 4: Tạo nội dung chi phí cận 0 làm sụp đổ sinh kế của người làm sáng tạo.
Đáp án: D.

q12.text: According to Paragraph 5, what separates true avant-garde art from AI outputs?
options: A. The ability to copy thousands of paintings rapidly
B. Conscious human rebellion that breaks accepted conventions
C. Using random noise rather than historical archives
D. Producing predictable images that match past public tastes

steps: Đoạn 5: Nghệ thuật tiên phong đòi hỏi sự nổi loạn phá bỏ quy tắc cũ của con người.
Đáp án: B.
